messages.focus:
A red-black tree is equivalent to a B-tree with t=2 (2-3-4 tree) when
you interpret black nodes as tree nodes and red nodes as “extra keys”
within a B-tree node.

messages.content:
A red-black tree with black height `h` corresponds to a 2-3-4 tree (B-tree with minimum degree `t=2`) of height `h`.

**The mapping:** Every node in the 2-3-4 tree (holding 1–3 keys) is "exploded" into a black node (the "backbone") with 0–2 red children hanging off it. The black node becomes the B-tree node's "primary" key, and red nodes represent the extra 1–2 keys that would share that same B-tree node.

**Why t=2?** A B-tree with `t=2` allows 1–3 keys per node (2–4 children). Correspondingly, the red-black tree rules allow any black node to have 0–2 red children attached, making 1–3 total keys in that "logical" B-tree node.

**Structural guarantees line up:**
- Red-black property (red nodes cannot have red children) ensures you never get 4 keys in one logical B-tree node.
- Equal black height on all paths maps to all B-tree leaves at the same depth.
- All B-tree operations (search, split, merge) map directly to red-black rotations and color flips.

This equivalence is why red-black trees are approximately balanced: a 2-3-4 tree has height `O(log n)`, so the exploded red-black tree has height at most `2·O(log n) = O(log n)` (since each B-tree level becomes at most 2 RB levels).
